blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Brookswood Real Estate Development Guide

items.t: SSMUH — Township Bylaw 6020, the rule this page must be read against (SETTLED): Bylaw No. 6020 (adopted November 18, 2024) amended Zoning Bylaw No. 2500 to allow small-scale multi-unit housing on eligible lots (inside the Urban Containment Boundary, connected to municipal water and sewer, no heritage designation, not in a Transit Oriented Area, lot not larger than 4,050 m²) — 3 units on lots of 280 m² or smaller, 4 units on larger eligible lots, lots over 4,050 m² ineligible, and NO 6-unit tier currently applies in the Township.

Zoning and lot sizes: Township Zoning Bylaw 1987 No. 2500 zones named in Township notices for the area include SR-1, SR-2, SR-3 and RU-2. Read from Bylaw 2500 Section 110.1 in Township council reports: SR-1 minimum lot area 3,716 m² and minimum frontage 40 m; SR-2 minimum 8,094 m² and 45 m; SR-3 minimum 1,765 m² and 27.45 m. RU-2 minimum lot area and frontage are UNVERIFIED from a readable bylaw section.

Presales (REDMA) — the frame for every developer sale named here: REDMA s. 21 gives a 7-day rescission period from the later of signing and acknowledging the disclosure statement, with deposits held in trust under s. 18. Bromley is selling as a presale with Phase 1 completion estimated Summer 2027 on the developer's sheet, so developer contracts there sit inside this frame.

ALR / second dwellings: the Agricultural Land Commission's housing rules permit one principal residence and, subject to conditions in the ALR Use Regulation, one additional residence, limited to 90 m² or less on parcels 40 ha or smaller and 186 m² or less on parcels larger than 40 ha. Township zoning for a second dwelling or coach house on non-reserve Brookswood acreage is UNVERIFIED. ALR residences cannot be stratified, so ALR parcels never become condo stock.

blocks.text: Good to know about Brookswood Real Estate Development Guide

items.t: (1) The page repeatedly presents a 6-plex tier for transit-adjacent lots ("Lots near frequent transit corridors may qualify for up to six units") — Bylaw No. 6020 contains no 6-unit tier and Transit Oriented Area lots are not SSMUH-eligible. (3) The page calls the Township "the last municipality in Metro Vancouver to act" on SSMUH — UNVERIFIED on any Township source.

The page has no feed — every number on it is editorial. Unlike the brookswood-guide and brookswood homes pages, this page carries no MLS listing feed and no listing cards; its six sections are argument, not inventory. A reader who treats its project names or statistics as listings or board data is misreading the page type.
The verified board shape behind the page's framing is a slow detached shelf.

The page frames every Brookswood property as having three values — as a home, as a building lot, and as part of an assembly — and states they do not always rank in that order, with creek greenway or SPEA setbacks able to make a property worth more as a home than as a lot. That framing is site copy, stated here as the page's position, not as a verified valuation rule.

Servicing decides what a lot can actually support. On acreage, the well and septic paper trail comes before any unit count: search GWELLS for the well record and ask for the Fraser Health record of sewerage system and letter of certification for the septic.

A neighbour's project is not your permission. The Brookswood-Fernridge plan lets previously undeveloped areas grow while protecting trees and watercourses, so a parcel's plan designation, neighbourhood plan (Booth, Fernridge or Rinn), zone minimums and ALR status — checked for the exact parcel — drive what can be built, not the project across the street.

items.t: SSMUH — Township Bylaw 6020 (adopted November 18, 2024) — and the 6-plex defect: 3 units on lots up to 280 m² and 4 units on larger eligible lots under 4,050 m²; eligibility requires the Urban Containment Boundary, municipal water and sewer, no heritage designation, and the lot must NOT be in a Transit Oriented Area; lots over 4,050 m² are ineligible, and NO 6-plex tier exists in Bylaw 6020.

ALR block (parcel status in Brookswood is parcel-specific and UNVERIFIED here; this page's blanket statement that "ALR properties are excluded entirely" is carried as page copy only, without the parcel-level caution): subdivision within the ALR requires Agricultural Land Commission approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)). Caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR.

faq.q: Can I build a fourplex on my Brookswood lot?
faq.a: Possibly — under Bylaw No. 6020 (adopted November 18, 2024), an eligible lot (inside the Urban Containment Boundary, on municipal water and sewer, no heritage designation, not in a Transit Oriented Area, 4,050 m² or smaller) permits 4 units if it is over 280 m² and 3 units at 280 m² or smaller. There is no 6-unit tier in the Township, whatever a listing or guide says about transit-adjacent lots.

The Brookswood-Fernridge Community Plan, with the Booth, Fernridge and Rinn Neighbourhood Plans under it; the Township states the plan allows previously undeveloped areas to grow while protecting trees and watercourses.

faq.q: Is a Brookswood property in the ALR?
faq.a: Some Township properties are in the Agricultural Land Reserve and some are not; check the exact parcel on the Agricultural Land Commission map and in the Township's GeoSource before making any development assumption — ALC rules permit one additional residence on ALR land only within its size caps and subject to Township bylaws.

faq.q: How do I find out which school serves an address in Brookswood?
faq.a: School catchments are set by address, so use the school district's catchment locator with the exact address. Catchment lines change, so check before you write an offer.

faq.q: Who can help me buy or sell in Brookswood?
faq.a: Jared Gibbons, REALTOR® with Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, works across the Fraser Valley and Metro Vancouver. Call or text 604-928-1361 or use the contact form on this site.

faq.q: Can I build a fourplex — or a sixplex — on my Brookswood lot?
faq.a: A fourplex, possibly: under Bylaw No. 6020 (adopted November 18, 2024), an eligible lot (inside the Urban Containment Boundary, on municipal water and sewer, no heritage designation, not in a Transit Oriented Area, 4,050 m² or smaller) permits 4 units if it is over 280 m² and 3 units at 280 m² or smaller. A sixplex, no — there is no 6-unit tier in the Township, whatever the live development page says about transit-adjacent lots; that page statement is a documented defect.

faq.q: Is there a list of Brookswood condo buildings I can buy into?
faq.a: No — and this page does not create one.

faq.q: The page names a 60-unit project and a 37-lot subdivision — can I price against them?
faq.a: Treat them as leads to verify with the Township, not as approvals.

faq.q: Are the page's market numbers ($2.35M median, 43 days, 92.6%, 4.7%) real?
faq.a: Price tempo off the verified board row, not the page's headline stats.
